questions.question: You need a managed feature store that supports both millisecond-latency lookups for real-time inference and full historical reads for offline training. Which AWS service component fits this requirement?
options: Amazon SageMaker Model Registry with versioned ModelPackageGroup entries kept in Amazon S3 buckets
Amazon SageMaker Feature Store with both online and offline stores enabled on the same feature group
Amazon DynamoDB streams replicated to Amazon Redshift through the AWS Database Migration Service
Amazon S3 partitioned Parquet datasets queried by AWS Glue and accessed by training jobs only
questions.explanation: SageMaker Feature Store provides two co-located stores per feature group: an online store for low-latency key-value lookups during inference and an offline store backed by S3 and queryable through Athena for training and analysis. They share schema and ingestion paths. Model Registry tracks model artifacts, not features. DynamoDB plus Redshift requires custom plumbing. S3-only loses the online lookup capability.

questions.question: A binary fraud-detection training set has 99.2% legitimate and 0.8% fraudulent transactions, and the trained classifier predicts 'legitimate' for nearly every input. Which technique most directly addresses the underlying class-imbalance problem?
options: Switch the loss function to mean squared error so larger residuals on rare classes are penalized more
Apply SMOTE to synthesize additional minority-class samples or use class weights during training
Replace stratified k-fold cross-validation with a single random 80/20 train/validation split of the data
Lower the learning rate by an order of magnitude so the optimizer takes smaller, more cautious updates
questions.explanation: SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique) generates new minority-class samples in feature space, and class weighting penalizes errors on the minority class more heavily — both are standard remedies for skewed labels. MSE is for regression and does not fix imbalance. Removing stratification makes evaluation worse, not better. A smaller learning rate does not change the underlying label distribution the model sees.

questions.question: You want SageMaker to automatically search a large hyperparameter space and converge near the optimum without an exhaustive grid sweep. Which tuning strategy is the recommended default?
options: Random search over the entire hyperparameter grid for the maximum configured number of training jobs
Bayesian optimization, which models the objective and chooses each next trial from prior trial results
A linear sweep that increments each hyperparameter by a fixed step until it reaches its upper bound
Manual tuning by a data scientist who launches jobs one at a time and inspects the validation metric
questions.explanation: SageMaker Automatic Model Tuning supports Bayesian (default), Random, Grid, and Hyperband strategies. Bayesian optimization builds a surrogate model of the objective and uses an acquisition function to pick informed next trials, typically converging in fewer jobs than random or grid search. Linear sweeps and manual tuning waste compute and do not learn from earlier trials.

questions.question: You want to cut deep-learning training cost by up to 90% on long-running SageMaker training jobs while tolerating possible interruptions. Which combination of settings is required?
options: Enable Managed Spot Training and configure CheckpointConfig so training resumes from the latest saved state
Use On-Demand instances and set MaxRuntimeInSeconds to a low value to keep the total job duration short
Enable Pipe input mode so streaming data input avoids re-downloading from Amazon S3 across attempts
Switch the framework container to inference-optimized images that disable gradient computation entirely
questions.explanation: Managed Spot Training uses EC2 Spot capacity for training instances, saving up to 90% over On-Demand. Spot interruptions are inevitable, so SageMaker requires a CheckpointConfig (an S3 prefix and a local checkpoint path) so the job can resume from the last checkpoint instead of restarting from scratch. Pipe mode improves throughput but does not handle interruptions, and inference images cannot perform training.

questions.question: Your team wants to train a custom PyTorch model with their own training script while still letting SageMaker handle infrastructure, data download, and artifact upload. Which approach matches the requirement most directly?
options: Bring Your Own Container with a fully custom Docker image, model server, and entrypoint built from scratch
Use a SageMaker built-in algorithm such as XGBoost and pass training hyperparameters through the SDK
Use a SageMaker pre-built PyTorch framework container in script mode with your script as the entry point
Run the script directly on an Amazon EC2 instance and copy the trained model artifacts to Amazon S3 by hand
questions.explanation: Script mode lets you reuse SageMaker's pre-built framework containers (PyTorch, TensorFlow, MXNet, Hugging Face, etc.) by supplying your own entry-point script through the Estimator's source_dir and entry_point arguments. SageMaker still manages instances, data channels, and artifact upload. BYOC is heavier than needed; built-in algorithms restrict you to their fixed interface; manual EC2 forfeits all managed benefits.

questions.question: A model needs to score 10 GB of accumulated daily transactions in a nightly batch with no requirement for an always-on endpoint. Which SageMaker inference option is the most appropriate choice?
options: Real-time inference endpoint provisioned 24/7 with auto-scaling enabled across two availability zones
Serverless Inference endpoint configured with a maximum concurrency of 200 simultaneous requests
Asynchronous Inference endpoint with input payloads pulled from an Amazon SQS queue continuously
Batch Transform job that reads inputs from Amazon S3, runs the model, and writes outputs back to S3
questions.explanation: Batch Transform is purpose-built for offline scoring of large datasets in S3 — it spins up compute, processes the input, writes results back to S3, then tears down. There are no idle endpoint costs. Real-time and Serverless target online traffic. Asynchronous Inference handles long-running single requests up to 1 GB, not bulk dataset scoring.

questions.question: You want to roll a new model version to 10% of live production traffic before deciding whether to promote it fully. Which SageMaker capability supports this with no client-side code changes?
options: Two SageMaker endpoints behind a custom Application Load Balancer that splits traffic via target groups
Production variants on a single endpoint with weights set so 10% of invocations route to the new model
Shadow tests that mirror 100% of production traffic to the candidate model and compare predictions offline
A SageMaker Pipeline step that retrains the model on every fifth request received by the existing endpoint
questions.explanation: A SageMaker endpoint can host multiple production variants behind one InvokeEndpoint URL. Setting initial_variant_weight on each variant routes traffic by weighted random allocation (for example 90/10), so clients use the same endpoint name with no SDK changes. A custom ALB adds infrastructure, shadow tests do not actually serve a user-traffic split, and Pipelines orchestrate workflows rather than request routing.

questions.question: You need a managed, lineage-tracked workflow that chains data processing, training, evaluation, conditional approval, and registration of an ML model. Which AWS service is purpose-built for this?
options: AWS Glue workflows orchestrated by Glue triggers and crawlers running on a recurring time schedule
Amazon SageMaker Pipelines with steps like ProcessingStep, TrainingStep, ConditionStep, and RegisterModel
Amazon EventBridge rules that invoke individual AWS Lambda functions based on event-bus pattern matching
AWS Step Functions executing arbitrary Lambda tasks defined in an Amazon States Language JSON definition
questions.explanation: SageMaker Pipelines is the native ML workflow service: it understands ML-specific step types (Processing, Training, Tuning, Condition, RegisterModel, etc.), captures lineage automatically in SageMaker Lineage, and integrates with the Model Registry. Glue and Step Functions can orchestrate generic tasks but lack ML-specific step abstractions and lineage. EventBridge handles event routing, not ML workflow orchestration.

questions.question: After deployment, the input feature distributions seen at the endpoint are drifting from the training distribution and accuracy is silently degrading. Which managed capability detects this most directly?
options: AWS CloudTrail event history filtered for SageMaker Runtime InvokeEndpoint API calls per minute
SageMaker Model Monitor with a data quality monitoring schedule comparing live captures to a baseline
Amazon CloudWatch metrics on the endpoint instance such as CPUUtilization and MemoryUtilization values
AWS X-Ray traces of the inference path showing per-request latency across container subsegments only
questions.explanation: SageMaker Model Monitor offers four monitor types: Data Quality (feature distribution drift), Model Quality (predictions vs. ground truth), Bias Drift, and Feature Attribution Drift. Each compares Data Capture from the endpoint to a baseline computed from the training set. CloudTrail audits API calls, CloudWatch surfaces infrastructure metrics, and X-Ray captures tracing — none of those detect statistical feature drift.

questions.question: To meet a compliance requirement, training jobs must not have direct internet egress, must use customer-managed KMS keys for storage, and must reach Amazon S3 over the AWS network. Which configuration satisfies all three?
options: Launch jobs in a public subnet and rely on the SageMaker control plane TLS for all data plane traffic
Enable VPC mode with EnableNetworkIsolation, use S3 VPC gateway endpoints, and pass a KMS KeyId to S3 outputs
Disable Data Capture entirely and store all training artifacts in an unencrypted, public-read S3 bucket
Run training on EC2 outside SageMaker with default-encrypted EBS volumes and an internet gateway attached
questions.explanation: SageMaker training jobs can be launched in a customer VPC with EnableNetworkIsolation set to true, which blocks the training container from any external network access except through configured VPC endpoints. An S3 VPC gateway endpoint keeps S3 traffic on the AWS backbone. Specifying a KmsKeyId on OutputDataConfig (and VolumeKmsKeyId on the resource config) enforces customer-managed encryption. The other options either expose traffic, drop encryption, or abandon SageMaker entirely.
